title: Minerals — Macro and Trace Elements
shortDescription: Functions, sources, bioavailability and deficiencies of key minerals.
genZNote: Calcium builds the squad, iron carries the oxygen, iodine runs the thermostat. Minerals = background cast that hold everything up.

sections.heading: Bioavailability and Metabolism
bullets: Heme iron (animal) absorbs better than non-heme iron; vitamin C enhances and phytates/tannins/calcium inhibit non-heme iron absorption.
Calcium absorption needs vitamin D; oxalates (spinach) and phytates reduce it.
Iodine from salt: WHO target salt iodisation; excess salt (>5 g/day advised limit) raises blood pressure.
Homeostasis: parathyroid hormone and calcitonin control blood calcium; hepcidin regulates iron.

Indian relevance: iron-deficiency anaemia is widespread (Anemia Mukt Bharat); fluorosis occurs in some groundwater areas, including parts of Gujarat; ICMR 2020 RDA for iron is higher for women of reproductive age.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Minerals are inorganic nutrients needed for structure, fluid balance and enzymatic functions; macro-minerals are needed in larger amounts than trace elements.
keyFacts: Heme iron absorbed better than non-heme iron.

highYieldFacts: Vitamin C enhances non-heme iron absorption.
commonTraps: Do not say iron is mainly absorbed in the large intestine — duodenum/jejunum.
